item.title: Cardinals’ Burleson takes aim at Roupp, Giants | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
The St. Louis Cardinals want left-handed slugger Alec Burleson to continue to be an everyday player who doesn’t get replaced against left-handed pitching.
This plan benefits the Cardinals only if Burleson produces against left- handers. He got a significant hit off a lefty Sunday — a go-ahead, three- run double in the sixth inning — to help the Cardinals beat the Chicago White Sox 3-1 and finish a series victory.
Ahead of his team’s next series, which will start tonight against the visiting San Francisco Giants, Cardinals manager Oli Marmol said Burleson is in a much better place now against southpaws than he was earlier in the season.

item.title: Burleson gives Cardinals win against White Sox with one swing | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description: Alec Burleson hit a go-ahead, bases-clearing double in the bottom of the sixth inning and Michael McGreevy pitched six effective innings Sunday afternoon for the St. Louis Cardinals in a 3-1 victory against the Chicago White Sox. Chicago put its first two runners aboard in the ninth inning and loaded the bases with two outs, but Colson Montgomery flied to medium center field against George Soriano. Montgomery also made a key error earlier that set up Burleson’s big hit.

item.title: Tolle’s immaculate first inning, Anthony’s hit lift Boston past Kansas City | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description: Roman Anthony’s two-out RBI single in the seventh inning snapped a tie at 1, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 4-1 win Sunday against the Kansas City Royals in the rain-delayed rubber game of their series. Willson Contreras, who missed the previous 12 games with a left hamstring strain, and Trevor Story each had two hits. Story had a two-RBI single in the eighth inning.

item.title: NFL Capsules: Bears score 59 in record-setting Week 1 win vs. Panthers | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description: Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more and the Chicago Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. In the teams’ season opener, D’Andre Swift scored three touchdown runs and rushed for 124 yards on 18 carries for Chicago. Williams completed 21-of-29 passes for 269 yards and added 65 rushing yards. Kyle Monangai gained 100 yards on 10 carries, including a 61-yard touchdown.

item.title: Murray’s Vikings debut cut short with concussion | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description: Kyler Murray saw his Minnesota Vikings debut come to an early end when he sustained a concussion on a scramble in the first quarter of Sunday afternoon’s game against the visiting Green Bay Packers. The former Arizona Cardinals quarterback took a hard hit to the side of his head and had his helmet knocked off as he slid short of the first-down marker with 6:10 to go in the opening quarter. He stayed on the turf while medical staff attended to him. Eventually, Murray got to his feet and walked to the locker room without assistance.
